Document Name.description:
Construct the **Document Name** from metadata in the document.

Format: "(artist_name) - (project_or_song_name) (execution_status)"
- Use project name if present; otherwise use song title(s).
- Multiple songs: comma-separate them.
- Execution status: FX (Fully-Executed), PX (Partially-Executed), NX (No Execution).

Return a single constructed string, e.g. "Drake - Certified Lover Boy FX".

IMPORTANT: Do NOT include prefixes like "Document Name:" — return only the constructed value.
Set "lines" to the line(s) containing the artist name and song/project title used to construct the value.

Execution Status.description:
Determine the **Execution Status** from the `signatures` array.

Count only parties with `signed: true` in `signatures` (SoundExchange is already excluded there).
- ALL signature-block parties signed → "FX"
- At least one signed but not all → "PX"
- None signed → "NX"

Return only: "FX", "PX", or "NX".
Set "lines" to the first line of the signature block.

signatures.description:
Scan the **signature block** at the end of the agreement. For each party with a designated signature line, return one entry.

A party is **signed** if their signature line contains: a handwritten name, a typed name below the line, "/s/ Name", an electronic signature, or any mark indicating execution. A party is **unsigned** if their signature line is blank or contains only a label (e.g. "By: ___").

EXCLUDE SoundExchange — do not include any SoundExchange LOD signature lines.

For "value", return the party's role or name as printed near the signature line (e.g. "Producer", "Label Representative", "John Smith, CEO").
Set "lines" to the line(s) of that party's signature line.
Set "signed" to true or false.

Song Title.description:
Extract the **Song Title(s)** from the agreement.

Locations: first 1-3 paragraphs ("master recording entitled '...'"), schedules, appendices, or tables.

Return ONLY the title(s) — not surrounding phrases. Multiple titles: comma-separate them.
Set "lines" to the line(s) where the titles themselves appear, not header lines.

Artist Name.description:
Extract the **Artist Name** — the professional/stage name (p/k/a).

Found in the first paragraph near ("Artist") or similar label. If both a legal name and a p/k/a are given, return ONLY the p/k/a.

Return ONLY the name — no quotes, labels, or legal names.
Set "lines" to the line where the name itself appears, not the line introducing it.

Single/Multisong Line.description:
Extract the **scope phrase** verbatim from the first two paragraphs indicating single-song, multi-song, or project scope.

Return ONLY what the document says, e.g. "Multi-Song arrangement" or "one (1) master recording". Do NOT append counts, track numbers, or any information not in the phrase itself.

Client Party.description:
Extract the **Client Party** name — the individual or entity addressed as "you" or "Producer" in the opening paragraph.

Return ONLY the name.

Direct Counterparty.description:
Extract the **Direct Counterparty** — the party issuing the agreement, referred to as "we", "us", or "Company".

Return ONLY the entity name.

Alternative Counterparties.description:
Extract names of any **Alternative Counterparties** — other entities involved beyond the direct counterparty.

Found in rights assignment clauses, revenue flow sections, SoundExchange LOD, Schedule A, or signature blocks.

Return a comma-separated list of entity names, or "not found".
Set "lines" to ONLY the lines containing the entity names, not the surrounding clause.

Classification of Recoupment Language.description:
Extract the **recoupment clause** — the language defining when the Producer becomes eligible for royalty payments.

Look for: "No royalty shall be payable until...", "After recoupment of Recording Costs...", "retroactively from record one after...".

Return the verbatim clause text, excluding section headers/numbers (e.g. omit "4.1.7 Classification of Recoupment Language.").

Effective Date.description:
Extract the **Effective Date** from the first paragraph.

If multiple dates on page 1, select the one labeled "Effective as of..." or "Effective Date:".

Return ONLY the date string.

Distributor.description:
Extract the **Distributor** name.

Look for: "distributed by [Entity]", "released by [Entity]", or "[Entity], a division of [Parent]".

If not explicitly stated, the Label and Distributor may be the same entity.

Return ONLY the entity name.

Label.description:
Extract the **parent company** that owns or controls the label in this agreement.

Look for: "[Label], a division of [Parent]", "owned by", "an imprint of", "subsidiary of".

Return ONLY the parent company name (e.g. "Warner Music Group", "Sony Music Entertainment").

Lawyer Information.description:
Extract **Lawyer Information** for both parties.

Look for: "C/O [Firm]", "represented by [Name]", address blocks near party names.

Return as: {"client_lawyer": "Name, Firm, Address", "counterparty_lawyer": "Name, Firm, Address"}.

Assign based on proximity to the Client Party / Producer name, or explicit labels like "Label's counsel".
If no lawyer info is found, return "not found".

Producer Royalty Points.description:
Extract the **initial/base Producer Royalty rate(s)** — one entry per base rate.

IMPORTANT: Only the INITIAL rate. Escalated/bump rates belong in **Bumps**. If "1.5% escalating to 2.0% after Gold", only return "1.5%" here.

Return the percentage only (e.g. "3%", "2.0%"). Do NOT append the royalty type — that belongs in Type of Royalty.
Do NOT combine multiple rates into one string — return one array entry per rate.

Type of Royalty.description:
Determine the **royalty calculation basis**. Only two valid values: "NAR" or "PPD".

**PPD (Published Price to Dealers):** The calculation base is a fixed price list, wholesale rate, or suggested retail price — NOT actual cash received. Trigger phrases: "Published Price to Dealers", "PPD", "Wholesale Price", "Base Royalty Rate", "Container or Packaging Deduction". Key signals: phantom deductions (fixed 20–25% subtracted for packaging/manufacturing regardless of actual cost), "Free Goods" clauses (e.g. 15% of units deemed non-royalty-bearing). Core formula pattern: (Unit Price − Fixed Deductions) × Royalty Rate.

**NAR (Net Actual Receipts):** The calculation base is actual cash flow — monies credited to the label from distributors or DSPs. Trigger phrases: "Net Actual Receipts", "NAR", "Net Artist Royalty", "Monies Received by Company", "Net Income", "Gross Receipts (less direct costs)", "Directly Attributable". Key signals: variable, itemized cost deductions (actual distribution fees, manufacturing costs, marketing out-of-pockets) subtracted before the producer percentage is applied. Core formula pattern: (Total Revenue − Actual Costs) × Producer %.

Return "NAR", "PPD", or "not found". Do not guess.
Set "lines" to the line where the royalty type or its defining formula/trigger phrase physically appears — not a section header.

Third Party Money.description:
Extract **Third Party Money** — amounts payable to the producer from third-party sources.

Return each as a SHORT value — just the amount (e.g. "$20,000", "9.47%"). Do NOT include surrounding context or section headers.

Organization Counting Units.description:
Check if the contract uses **USNRC** (U.S. Normal Retail Channels) for measuring sales.

Look for: "USNRC Net Sales", "Net Sales (USNRC)", "sales through U.S. Normal Retail Channels".

Return "USNRC" or "not found".

Producer Advance Legal Recoupment.description:
Extract the **Producer Advance amount** — the dollar value only.

Look near: "Producer Advance", "Advance payable to Producer", "Advance of $X".

Return ONLY the monetary value (e.g. "$10,000").
Set "lines" to the line where the dollar amount appears, not the header line.

Scope signal (for `advance_scope` in song entries): if one advance amount is stated globally with no per-song breakdown → agreement-level. If distinct amounts are stated per track in a schedule or table → song-level.

Recoupment Classification.description:
Extract the **Recoupment Classification** — how the advance is recouped.

Valid values: "Non-Returnable Recoupable", "Partially-Recoupable", "Fully-Recoupable".

Found adjacent to the advance amount. Return ONLY one of the three values above, or "not found".

Legal Advance.description:
Extract the **Legal Advance** amount — the dollar value paid for legal fees.

Look near: "legal advance", "advance for legal fees", "contribution toward legal costs".

Return ONLY the monetary value (e.g. "$5,000").
Set "lines" to the line where the dollar amount appears, not the header line.

Bumps.description:
Extract the **full royalty escalation schedule (Bumps)** — ALL tiers including the base rate.

Return the complete schedule verbatim, e.g. "Base: 3.5% NAR; Gold (500K): 4.0% NAR; Platinum (1M): 4.5% NAR".

Include every tier listed (base through highest). Set "lines" to ALL lines containing the schedule.
